isolation.statement: Fresh primitive-only adjudication used the frozen v2.7 rules, locked excerpts, target packets, component graphs, and burden routes; no legacy material or numerical scores were available.

annotations.coverageRationale: This is a constructive clinical and spiritual-practice claim, so opponent-target coverage axes do not apply.
annotations.mechanismRationale: No opponent demand is diagnosed or reframed; the move directly proposes a combined practical method.
annotations.burdenRationale: The proposed scientific and spiritual method supports the con side's central practical-flourishing bridge.

annotations.coverageRationale: This constructive definition of active personal theism has no locked opponent target for coverage classification.
annotations.mechanismRationale: The move states Koukl's creator and rescue-plan view without diagnosing or replacing an opponent demand.
annotations.burdenRationale: An active personal creator directly supports the pro side's central objective-purpose and divine-relationship bridge.

annotations.coverageRationale: This is a constructive statement of partial participation and intended friendship, so target axes are inapplicable.
annotations.mechanismRationale: No opponent claim is criticized; the move independently explains degrees of purpose under Koukl's view.
annotations.burdenRationale: Creator-given purpose and friendship with God directly support the pro side's central burden bridge.

annotations.coverageRationale: O'Connor constructively states the mortality problem and therefore has no opponent target for coverage axes.
annotations.mechanismRationale: The move introduces an existential mechanism rather than diagnosing or reframing an opponent's argument.
annotations.burdenRationale: The mortality account supplies a central secular explanation of the human search for subjective meaning.

scopeEvidence.text: It's not enough to address what people really want

evidence.text: It's not just even some kind of purpose which is given to you by an authoritative creative source

defectEvidence.text: It's not just even some kind of purpose which is given to you by an authoritative creative source

impactEvidence.text: It's not enough to address what people really want

annotations.coverageRationale: O'Connor retains creator-assigned purpose but strengthens the adequacy standard to what people really want, distinguishing assignment from sufficiency while leaving friendship unaddressed.
annotations.mechanismRationale: He identifies a scope mismatch between having assigned purpose and having enough meaning, with the stated consequence that assignment does not address the relevant human demand.
annotations.burdenRationale: Showing that authoritative assignment alone is insufficient directly advances the con side's central account of meaningful flourishing.

evidence.text: a lot of people who are making paper clips are not satisfied with it
a lot of people who are making paper clips are not satisfied with it
If God decides that he wants to make creatures to be in friendship with him because this reflects his loving character

defectEvidence.text: If God decides that he wants to make creatures to be in friendship with him because this reflects his loving character

impactEvidence.text: I don't see how that is somehow negligible or arbitrary at all

annotations.coverageRationale: Koukl accepts the paperclip case's dissatisfaction but distinguishes arbitrary production from loving friendship, directly operating on every locked component.
annotations.mechanismRationale: The loving-character difference attacks the paperclip comparison's support, and Koukl expressly concludes that the divine purpose is not thereby arbitrary or negligible.
annotations.burdenRationale: The loving-friendship distinction directly supports the pro side's central objective-purpose route against the analogy.

evidence.text: the theology that they believe is true is going to affect their feelings and their experience

defectEvidence.text: human beings are just an illusion

impactEvidence.text: this is going to convey a whole different experience that they have

annotations.coverageRationale: Koukl preserves the content-versus-satisfaction issue, distinguishes theological views of persons, and denies that content is experientially inert, but does not address expected happiness itself.
annotations.mechanismRationale: The illusion-versus-significant-individual contrast challenges cross-religion comparability and explicitly links the difference to a different lived experience.
annotations.burdenRationale: Arguing that theological truth-content affects experience directly advances the pro side's central relationship-and-flourishing route.

evidence.text: there are people who do the opposite there
I went from Christianity to Islam

defectEvidence.text: there are people who do the opposite there

annotations.coverageRationale: The reverse-conversion counterexample attacks both the one-way anecdotal premise and its use against religious interchangeability, contacting the entire packet.
annotations.mechanismRationale: O'Connor supplies contrary cases that expose evidential insufficiency, but the short reply does not explicitly state the resulting inferential consequence.
annotations.burdenRationale: Counterexamples to uniquely Christian satisfaction support the con side's central claim that flourishing is not exclusive to Christian theism.

objectEvidence.text: I'm using dharma and that's what people will like put morality onto dharma, where I I don't think that that's actually fair

annotations.coverageRationale: Kanojia changes the referent from Koukl's transcendent objective morality to dharma and disputes projecting Western morality onto that distinct concept.
annotations.mechanismRationale: The move marks a framework difference but does not explicitly diagnose a qualifying defect in the locked objective-morality packet.
annotations.burdenRationale: Distinguishing dharma from Western moral categories supports the con side's broader spiritual-practice alternative at the central level.

evidence.text: doing your dharma is basically the way I would describe your dharma is when I throw a ball in the air, it comes down
whether it's common sensical depends on what's common

defectEvidence.text: these concepts I don't think are one-to-one

impactEvidence.text: whether it's common sensical depends on what's common

annotations.coverageRationale: Kanojia distinguishes dharma's regularity from moral ought and attacks the universality of the commonsense category.
annotations.mechanismRationale: He identifies non-equivalent concepts and states that the commonsense inference depends on what a culture makes common.
annotations.burdenRationale: The dharma distinction advances the con side's central alternative framework for duty and meaningful practice.

evidence.text: there is an a layer of morality, but that is not within dharma

defectEvidence.text: there is an a layer of morality, but that is not within dharma

impactEvidence.text: there's a set of different things that we would generally speaking call morality

annotations.coverageRationale: Kanojia directly denies that his account lacks morality and distinguishes the morality layer from dharma, contacting both attribution components.
annotations.mechanismRationale: He corrects the attributed view and identifies truthfulness and nonviolence as the resulting distinct moral category.
annotations.burdenRationale: A differentiated but real moral layer supports the con side's central claim that non-Christian practices can guide flourishing.

objectEvidence.text: I don't want to kill my cousins, and I don't want to kill my teacher

annotations.coverageRationale: The move changes from the emergency-room duty to the Mahabharata killing case, so it substitutes a different subject rather than contacting those components.
annotations.mechanismRationale: Because the response substitutes the Mahabharata subject, it does not diagnose a qualifying defect in the locked emergency-room target packet.
annotations.burdenRationale: The counterexample supports the con side's central case for a distinct spiritual framework of duty and flourishing.

objectEvidence.text: All I'm saying is that it is unexpected if Christianity were true that that suffering would be as it is

burdenEvidence.text: I'm not saying that on my worldview that suffering is wrong and must be fixed and there's some moral element

malformedDemandEvidence.text: I'm not saying that on my worldview that suffering is wrong and must be fixed and there's some moral element

replacementDemandEvidence.text: All I'm saying is that it is unexpected if Christianity were true that that suffering would be as it is

annotations.coverageRationale: O'Connor disowns the external moral-assessment demand and replaces it with Christianity's internal predictive question, changing question type and burden.
annotations.mechanismRationale: The substituted target has no locked-target defect; separately, he explains the moral demand as malformed and states a replacement predictive test.
annotations.burdenRationale: The internal suffering prediction directly advances the con side's central truth-evidence objection to Christian purpose claims.

evidence.text: she was capable of initiating a free action
You don't have to have in a certain sense deterministic element in your in your soul that forces you to act a certain way

defectEvidence.text: You don't have to have in a certain sense deterministic element in your in your soul that forces you to act a certain way

impactEvidence.text: she was capable of initiating a free action

annotations.coverageRationale: Koukl preserves the regress target, denies that Eve's act required a prior proclivity, and undermines the conclusion through free initiation, leaving the offered fall explanation untouched.
annotations.mechanismRationale: He identifies the missing necessity premise that action requires a determining proclivity and states that Eve could instead initiate a free action.
annotations.burdenRationale: The free-action explanation supports the pro side's central theistic response to suffering and moral agency.

objectEvidence.text: the fall does not explain the proclivity to sin because Eve already had it

scopeEvidence.text: It also doesn't explain the origin of suffering

annotations.coverageRationale: O'Connor changes from what Eve knew and did to what the fall explains, while strengthening the explanatory range through evil and suffering origins.
annotations.mechanismRationale: Because the response changes to a broader explanatory question, it does not diagnose a defect against the preserved locked target packet.
annotations.burdenRationale: The alleged explanatory failure directly advances the con side's central suffering and truth-evidence objection.

objectEvidence.text: if your world view does not have a way of making sense or our moral intuitions about suffering, even animal suffering, it's not an adequate world view

burdenEvidence.text: if your world view does not have a way of making sense or our moral intuitions about suffering, even animal suffering, it's not an adequate world view

annotations.coverageRationale: Koukl changes the question from Christianity's prediction to naturalism's moral adequacy and reassigns that demand to O'Connor.
annotations.mechanismRationale: He identifies the absence of moral ramifications and explicitly concludes that a worldview missing them is inadequate.
annotations.burdenRationale: The moral-intuition adequacy test directly advances the pro side's central moral-grounding bridge.
